P2:
Enable: Workspace > Server Authority, set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (full release July 2026).
It forces: NextGenerationReplication enabled, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem enabled, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled on, UseFixedSimulation enabled.
Predicted gameplay logic: put it in a ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage that both client and server require, and register it with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn) so it runs in the fixed simulation step on both sides (client predicts, server is authoritative and corrects/rolls back). Read input via InputAction (Input Action System); keep custom predicted state in attributes (first 64 replicate; names/strings max 50 chars).
Clock: use time() (simulation time), not tick(), os.clock() or os.time().
Gotchas: no Destroy/reparenting inside bound simulation functions; RenderStepped cosmetic VFX must tolerate mispredictions/rollback.

- Games can no longer read message text: TextChatMessage.Text and .Translation return "" (with a warning); OnIncomingMessage and Player.Chatted give no text; PrefixText is unsupported (prefixes/role badges not back until ~Feb 2027).

P5:
Since 2026-07-29 limits are per experience, per minute, shared by all servers plus Open Cloud (base raised from 250 to 300):
- Read (Get): 300 + 40 x CCU
- Write (Set/Update/Increment): 300 + 20 x CCU
- List: 300 + 2 x CCU
- Remove: 300 + 40 x CCU
UpdateAsync counts as 1 read + 1 write (consumes both budgets).
Per key (rolling 60 s): 25 MB read, 4 MB write throughput, each request rounded up to the next KB. Request queue per server holds 30; overflow errors 301-306.
Storage: 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime unique players, counting the latest version of each key, compressed.
Check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before bursts; Open Cloud migration jobs spend the same live budget. Use UpdateAsync with session locking, not GetAsync+SetAsync.

G1:
Rules:
1. Set MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt exactly once, in one server script.
2. Return PurchaseGranted ONLY after the grant is durably saved; return NotProcessedYet on any failure, if the player isn't in the server, or if data isn't loaded - Roblox retries later (on next join).
3. Be idempotent: record receipt.PurchaseId (in the player's saved data or a purchase-history store, via UpdateAsync) and if already processed just return PurchaseGranted without granting again.
4. Wrap DataStore calls in pcall; never yield forever; never error out of the callback.
5. Look up the product by ProductId on the server; never trust client info.
Why charged-but-nothing: callback returned PurchaseGranted even though the save failed or player was nil (or errored silently). Why double grant: no PurchaseId dedupe - a retried receipt (after timeout/rejoin, or callback returning NotProcessedYet after already granting) grants again, or GetAsync+SetAsync races overwrite.
G2:
Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old one or multiple servers might write the same key (session locking, currency increments, receipts, teleports/rejoins). SetAsync blindly overwrites and can clobber newer data written by another server; GetAsync+SetAsync is a race.
Transform function rules:
- Must be pure and fast: no yielding (no waits, no other DataStore/HTTP calls), no side effects (don't grant items or fire remotes inside it) - it may be called multiple times on retry/conflict.
- Treat the old value as possibly nil (new player) and don't mutate it unexpectedly; return the new value.
- Return nil to cancel the write (e.g. lock owned by another server, stale version).
- Check session lock / version inside it before writing.
Also: wrap in pcall; UpdateAsync costs 1 read + 1 write of budget.
G3:
Not safe. typeof(gold)=="number" accepts NaN and inf and fractions. NaN fails every comparison, so `gold < 0` and `gold > Gold.Value` are both false and NaN passes; fractional/huge precision values pass too. Also the balance isn't reserved, so a player can create many offers (or spend the gold) totalling more than they own, and there's no rate limit.
Fix:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold then return end -- NaN
  if gold ~= math.floor(gold) or gold < 1 or gold > 1e9 then return end
  if not canAct(player) then return end -- cooldown
  if gold > player.Gold.Value - reservedGold(player) then return end
  reserve(player, gold)  -- escrow; deduct atomically on trade accept
  createOffer(player, gold)
end)
```
Re-validate balance server-side when the trade completes; keep the balance in server data, not a client-writable value.
G4:
The Animator overwrites Motor6D.Transform every step for every joint a playing track keys, and it steps after Heartbeat-time writes are applied, so your Heartbeat aim is replaced by the idle pose. Transform is meant to be set per frame after animation.
Fix: write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (runs after the Animator has stepped, before physics/render), each frame, composing with the animated value instead of replacing it: motor.Transform = aimCF * animated (aim in parent space), or animated * offset for a local twist, or animated:Lerp(target, w) for fades. Don't do Transform = Transform * offset on joints no track keys (compounds every frame). Alternatively remove the barrel joint from the idle animation.
Edit C0/C1 instead for persistent rest offsets (mounting angle, default pose, grip) that should apply under every animation - the Animator never touches C0/C1. Avoid per-frame C0 writes for animation (replicates/fights).
G5:
Priority is resolved per joint: a track only competes on joints it actually keys. Enum.AnimationPriority order: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4. The highest-priority track(s) keying a joint take their weight first; lower priorities only get the remaining weight (1 - higher weight). So walk (Movement) + swing (Action, weight 1) -> swing fully controls the arm. If the swing is also Movement/Core (e.g. default priority in the editor) it blends 50/50 with walk -> weak swing; if swing weight is 0.6, walk gets 0.4. Equal-priority tracks blend proportionally to their weights; total weight below 1 blends toward the rest pose.
Fix: set the swing's priority to Action (or higher) - animTrack.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action before Play, or in the Animation Editor - and play with weight 1 (track:Play(fadeTime, 1)). Load the track once and reuse it.
G6:
Unit mismatch: Blender works in metres (1 unit) while FBX stores centimetres; with default settings the FBX unit scale/scale factor gets applied so 1 Blender unit becomes ~100 Studio units (studs), or several scale fixes stack. Roblox treats 1 unit = 1 stud.
Recommended FBX export: Apply Scalings = 'FBX Unit Scale' (all other scales 1.0) - or alternatively Transform Scale 0.01 / scene Unit Scale 0.01, but use only ONE method; apply transforms first (Ctrl+A scale 1, rotation 0), origin at the model root; Forward = -Z/Z per rig convention, Up = Y; Add Leaf Bones off; Bake Animation simplify 0; selected objects only. Don't fix it by rescaling in Studio for rigs (animation translations stay in old units). GLB export doesn't need the scale fix.
G7:
Modifiers are non-destructive in Blender; the glTF exporter only exports the base mesh unless 'Apply Modifiers' (Include/Data > Mesh > Apply Modifiers) is enabled, which is off by default. So Mirror's other half and Bevel's geometry aren't in the file. Fix: tick Apply Modifiers in the glTF export (Armature modifier is skipped, so skinning still works), or apply the modifiers manually.
Catch: with Apply Modifiers on, the exporter drops shape keys (morph targets) - so for meshes with shape keys (e.g. facial/FACS heads) apply Mirror/Bevel manually on a copy (or before creating shape keys) instead. Also expect a higher triangle count from Bevel; keep the export setting consistent across the team.
G8:
1) Scale sizing: fromScale(0.3,0.3) is 30% of width and 30% of height of the screen, so on screens with different aspect ratios the frame's ratio changes (stretch/squash). Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = desired ratio, e.g. 1), or size by one axis with SizeConstraint = RelativeYY/RelativeXX; optionally UISizeConstraint/UITextSizeConstraint for min/max.
2) Safe area: by default the ScreenGui lays out in the area including the device insets and top bar region; a top-left button can sit under the notch/Roblox top bar. Fix: ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets (avoids notch and Roblox CoreUI top bar; DeviceSafeInsets for just the notch), keep IgnoreGuiInset = false, and add margin/offset from the corner. Use full-screen insets (ScreenInsets = None) only for decorative backgrounds in a separate ScreenGui.

```lua
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local Items = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemCatalog) -- [id] = {price=...}
local Data = require(game.ServerScriptService.PlayerData)
local last = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
  if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or typeof(quantity) ~= "number" then return end
  if quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 or quantity < 1 or quantity > 99 then return end
  local item = Items[itemId]; if not item then return end
  local now = os.clock()
  if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.3 then return end
  last[player] = now
  local profile = Data.get(player); if not profile then return end
  local cost = item.price * quantity -- server-side price only
  if profile.Coins < cost then return end
  profile.Coins -= cost
  profile.Inventory[itemId] = (profile.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
  Data.replicate(player)
end)
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
Never trust client price/balance; validate types, NaN, ints, bounds, existence; rate-limit; deduct and grant in one synchronous step.
T2:
```lua
-- key "Player_<UserId>" = {lock={jobId, t}, data={...}}
local function load(player)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, res = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
      old = old or {data = defaultData()}
      local l = old.lock
      if l and l.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - l.t < 1800 then
        return nil -- locked by another server: cancel
      end
      old.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, t = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and res and res.lock.jobId == game.JobId then
      sessions[player] = res.data; return true
    end
    task.wait(attempt * 2) -- other server still saving
  end
  player:Kick("Data busy, rejoin") ; return false
end

local function save(player, release)
  local d = sessions[player]; if not d then return end
  pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
    if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end
    old.data = d
    old.lock = (not release) and {jobId = game.JobId, t = os.time()} or nil
    return old
  end)
end
-- autosave every ~60s (refreshes lock t); PlayerRemoving -> save(p, true);
-- BindToClose -> save all with release, wait for completion.
-- Before teleport: save(p, true) and finish it before TeleportAsync.
```
Key ideas: only the lock holder writes; stale locks expire; never use SetAsync; receipts/trades recorded inside the locked data.

T4:
FireServer automatically passes the firing player as the first argument to OnServerEvent. By also passing LocalPlayer, the server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50), so `amount` is the Player Instance and amount + 1 errors.
Fix the client: `remote:FireServer(50)`. Server stays `function(player, amount)`. Also validate on the server: `if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end` - and don't trust the client for amounts that grant currency (the server should decide values).
T5:
Race: in Studio solo play the player joins very quickly, often before the server Script has run and connected PlayerAdded, so the event already fired for that player and your handler never runs for them (live servers usually start scripts before anyone joins). Also any yield before the Connect (WaitForChild, require, DataStore calls) widens the gap.
Standard fix: connect, then loop over players already in game:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
  local ls = Instance.new("Folder"); ls.Name = "leaderstats"
  local c = Instance.new("IntValue"); c.Name = "Coins"; c.Parent = ls
  ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Connect before any yields.

```lua
local BadgeService = game:GetService("BadgeService")
local BADGE_ID = 123456

local function awardFinishBadge(player: Player)
  -- check ownership first (avoid wasted calls); retry briefly
  local okHas, has = pcall(BadgeService.UserHasBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
  if okHas and has then return true end
  for attempt = 1, 3 do
    local ok, result = pcall(BadgeService.AwardBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
    if ok then return result end -- true if awarded
    warn(("AwardBadgeAsync failed (%d): %s"):format(attempt, tostring(result)))
    if not player.Parent then return false end
    task.wait(attempt * 2)
  end
  return false
end
```
Call it from the server when the finish is validated server-side (e.g. finish-line Touched + checkpoint check), never from a client remote alone. AwardBadgeAsync is the 2026 name (AwardBadge deprecated but still works); badge must be enabled and belong to this experience.

T8: Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs (mesh streaming / improved LoD system) is enabled in your place - when it is on, the engine manages mesh LoD itself and ignores MeshPart.RenderFidelity entirely, so Precise vs Automatic makes no difference and distant meshes still get lower LoDs. Check that Workspace property first. Fixes: accept engine LoD (set RenderFidelity to Automatic everywhere; it is the recommended value), make the source mesh's silhouette robust to decimation and keep it reasonable (<20k tris), or for the old behaviour disable MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs (if still allowed). Note Model.LevelOfDetail (StreamingMesh/SLIM) is separate and applies only with StreamingEnabled. Also verify the published place actually has the change saved/published (Studio vs live).
